conclusion: AMDGPU target spelling and ELF symbol visibility are producer/linker provenance details, not ISA-execution proof: the pinned Triton image uses amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-unknown-gfx950 and a DEFAULT-visible descriptor while the pinned RDC fixtures use the double-hyphen gfx950 spelling and PROTECTED descriptors.
decision: Accept the unknown-gfx950 spelling and DEFAULT descriptor only under the exact Triton metadata-only branch, keep the code symbol GLOBAL PROTECTED, preserve the stricter RDC checks, and leave isa_supported_by_gemsim=false.
invalidated_assumptions: All conforming gfx950 producers emit one byte-identical amdhsa.target spelling.
Accepting a DEFAULT-visible descriptor implies that the image is executable in GemSim.
observation: The exact 5,408-byte vecadd HSACO validates only after recognizing its unknown-gfx950 target and GLOBAL DEFAULT vecadd.kd; the same record remains metadata-only, requires code-object transport, and reports no GemSim ISA support.
question_or_symptom: Why did a source-pinned Triton vecadd HSACO fail the existing RDC-oriented parser despite carrying gfx950 metadata?
